newsitem.title: USA: Georgia job growth to moderate, forecast says.
newsitem.headline: Georgia job growth to moderate, forecast says.

text.p: Georgia's post-Olympic economic slump has begun to dissipate, but the state's job growth should continue to moderate through 1999, according to a quarterly forecast by Georgia State University Thursday.

Slower economic activity and the difficult comparisons with the pre-Olympic buildup have eroded state revenues. Revenues growth is expected to reach 5.6 percent for 1997 and then slow to 5 percent in each of the next two years.

"Fortunately, reduced capital gains taxation at the federal level will increase transactions, raising increased revenues in Georgia. Even so, little growth is expected in the next two years," economist Donald Ratajczak said.
Georgia should create 71,100 new jobs in 1997 but only 58,900 in 1998 and 51,100 in 1999, Ratajczak said.
Atlanta's economy should experience similar slowing with job gains of 52,300 in 1997, 50,800 in 1998 and 35,000 in 1999, Ratajczek predicted.
Employment remains strong in the cities but jobs are declining outside the metropolitan areas, the report said.

In March, nearly 1,800 fewer jobs existed outside the cities, while 75,000 were created inside. Every metro area in Georgia currently is expanding, although Columbus' 1.1 percent job gain and Augusta's 2.4 percent gain were below average for the state.
A tight labor market has driven unemployment to only 3.7 percent in Atlanta and 4.5 percent in Georgia this year.

Gradual increases in unemployment along with a slowing in population gains are expected in Atlanta and statewide through 1999, Ratajczak said. Atlanta's population growth rate peaked at 3.2 percent in 1994 and should slow to only 2.6 percent by 1999.
No recession is expected in either Georgia or the United States during the forecast period, but favorable policies and a declining dollar against other currencies are needed to achieve that outcome.
"Otherwise, a needed correction in housing activity will spread to the trade, transportation services and business services by the end of 1998," Ratajczak said.
